title: [2026-10-01] feat: retire MAI Image 2.5 Flash into 2.6 alias
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Retires the separate MAI Image 2.5 Flash catalog entry and Azure route; its old ID resolves to `microsoft/mai-image-2.6-flash`. Keeps Azure East US `MAI-Image-2.6-Flash`, multiplier 0.75, Quest access, and no fallback. Azure confirms 36 deployment RPM; per-user limit stays 12.
- Resolves current-main conflicts and replaces the outdated upcoming-change announcement with the completed cutover notice.
- Verified October 1: 85 focused Gen tests, Enter price snapshot, both typechecks, Biome; real local old-ID generation at 768²/1536², editing, invalid-input rejection, cache reuse, and staging usage/billing reconciliation. Seeded disconnect/rejoin returns identical bytes, one wallet debit and one billed event. Authenticated production 2.6 generation/cache probe passes.
- Rollout: alias-aware authorization remains required. Updated read-only audit: 654 production keys and 0 staging keys store the old ID. Run a separate permissions cleanup after deployment and prove zero remaining references.
- Corrects public width/height descriptions to the existing 2.6 Flash limits. Existing unseeded image requests choose a new cache identity; disconnect/rejoin validation used an explicit seed. Pre-existing Content Safety host no longer resolves in dev/production configuration; secrets unchanged. Azure generation succeeds and moderation regressions pass.

gist.headline: Flash gets a new name
gist.blurb: The old MAI Image 2.5 Flash ID leads to 2.6 Flash instead of its own Azure route. Existing requests keep working; the catalog has one less nearly identical signpost.
gist.summary: The MAI Image 2.5 Flash ID becomes an alias for `microsoft/mai-image-2.6-flash`, consolidating generation on the Azure East US 2.6 Flash deployment while retaining Quest access, a 0.75 multiplier, and the per-user limit of 12.
gist.impact: Requests using the old ID resolve to 2.6 Flash, and the public width and height descriptions reflect 2.6 Flash’s existing limits.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the MAI image-model cutover as two small pixel signposts: the old 2.5 Flash ID points toward a single glowing 2.6 Flash image-making easel. Polli, wearing a tiny painter’s beret, guides the sign into place; a friendly CRT monitor robot admires the generated picture, with code-plants and flowers around them.
